subject: physics
question_text: Develop the notions of work and kinetic energy and show that it leads to the work-energy theorem.

verification.note: Sri Chaitanya IPE Junior Fastrack (Rev. May 2024), Unit 6 LONG ANSWER — and the TSBIE Basic Learning Material carries the same question in its own Unit 6 Long Answer set, so both sources agree this is an 8-mark form. The split across the steps is invented and needs a Telangana IPE teacher; no exam appearance years are printed, so appearances[] stays empty.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.label: Work
lines: the dot product of the force and the

lines.text: W = F · S = F S cos θ

steps.margin_note: Definition, formula, then the three cases. The cases are half the marks here.
steps.why: Work is a scalar built from two vectors, so only the part of the force along the motion counts. The three cases are just cos θ at its three special values.
common_mistakes: Writing W = F × S as a cross product. Work is a DOT product and is a scalar.

recall.must_convey: That work is the dot product F·S = F S cos θ, with positive, zero and negative cases.
accept: work is the dot product of force and displacement
W equals F S cos theta
theta zero positive, ninety zero, one eighty negative
dot product ye work
reject: kinetic energy is half m v squared

steps.memory_tip: Work = F s cos θ — the cos θ is what makes zero and negative work possible.

steps.label: Kinetic energy
lines: the energy possessed by a body by
steps.margin_note: "By virtue of its motion" is the phrase. Potential energy is the one about position.
steps.why: This is the quantity the theorem will connect the work to, so it has to be defined before the proof can mean anything.
common_mistakes: Writing KE = mv² without the half.

recall.must_convey: That kinetic energy is the energy due to motion, KE = ½mv².
accept: energy because of its motion
KE is half m v squared
motion valla vachhe energy
reject: work is the dot product of force and displacement

steps.memory_tip: Define KE before the proof: ½mv², the energy a body has because it moves.

steps.label: The set-up
steps.margin_note: One block, twice: u at A, v at B, F pushing, S between them. Everything the proof uses is in this picture.
steps.why: The proof mixes a kinematics equation with a force equation, and the figure is what shows they describe the same journey.
common_mistakes: Drawing the block but not marking S, so F S has no distance to refer to.

recall.must_convey: That a figure is drawn of the body moving from A to B under F, with u, v and S marked.
accept: draw the block moving from A to B
mark u v and S
figure with force and displacement
reject: W equals half m v squared minus half m u squared

steps.memory_tip: Draw the block pushed from A to B: force F, distance S, speeds u and v at the two ends.

steps.label: The theorem
lines: The work done by the net force acting
on a body is equal to the change in its
steps.margin_note: State it before proving it. And say NET force — the theorem is false for one force among several.
steps.why: The word "net" is what makes it exact. Friction and the applied force each do work; only their sum equals the change in kinetic energy.
common_mistakes: Leaving out "net", which makes the statement wrong whenever more than one force acts.

recall.must_convey: That the work done by the net force equals the change in kinetic energy.
accept: work done by the net force equals change in kinetic energy
net force chese work KE change ki equal
reject: kinetic energy is half m v squared

steps.memory_tip: The statement needs the word NET: net work = change in kinetic energy.

steps.label: The proof
lines: Let the body move from A to B through a
distance S, from velocity u to v.
The work done is W = F S, and F = ma,
steps.margin_note: Two ingredients, named: the kinematics equation and F = ma. Then substitute — do not skip to the answer.
steps.why: The S cancels, which is why the result depends only on the speeds and not on how far it took to change them.
common_mistakes: Using F = ma but never writing W = F S, so there is nothing to substitute into.

recall.must_convey: That a is found from v² − u² = 2aS and substituted into W = F S = maS.
accept: v squared minus u squared equals two a S
W equals F S equals m a S
substitute a into the work
a ni substitute cheyyali
reject: work done by the net force equals change in kinetic energy

steps.memory_tip: Combine v² − u² = 2aS with F = ma. Multiply, and the S cancels.

steps.label: The result
lines: that is, W = final KE − initial KE.
Hence the work-energy theorem is proved.
steps.margin_note: Say the last line in words as well as symbols — that sentence IS the theorem you stated earlier.
steps.why: The proof closes only when the algebra is named back as the statement it set out to show.
common_mistakes: Stopping at the algebra without linking it back to the theorem.

recall.must_convey: That W = ½mv² − ½mu², the change in kinetic energy, proving the theorem.
accept: W equals half m v squared minus half m u squared
final KE minus initial KE
theorem is proved

insider_note: The word NET in the statement is checked — net work equals the change in kinetic energy.
